issues.note: Per-bot mutex DESIGNED CORRECTLY in plugins/landfolk/landfolk/orchestrator/mutex_key.py: [bot:<name>] title prefix yields key bot:<name>. The enforcement gap was that dispatch_once (core Hermes) calls recompute_ready which promotes ALL eligible todos → ready in one shot, ignoring mutex_key. The dispatcher's claim loop then claimed them all before the NEXT gate-check could park duplicates. FIX (2026-06-09): added gate.gate_check Step 5b that pre-parks excess eligible todos by writing claim_lock=mutex_park:KEY while they're still in todo status. recompute_ready only touches `status`, so the lock survives the todo→ready flip, and the dispatcher's `WHERE claim_lock IS NULL` selector skips parked siblings.

evidence.observation: Three concurrent build cards mid-run: t_a1d8ad7c + t_acb2c6c9 both [bot:mox], t_9c2d96f4 [bot:pip]. Per-bot serialization required for road tier.
mutex_key.mutex_key(assignee=builder-mox, title=[bot:mox] [BUILD] clear segment 2) returns bot:mox correctly; same for segment 4. Both still ran concurrently. Enforcement gap, not key gap.

Root cause traced to dispatch_once line 6046 calling recompute_ready WITHOUT mutex awareness. Fixed via landfolk gate.py Step 5b (pre-park todos). 8 new tests in test_mutex_todo_pre_park.py cover the race scenario end-to-end: 3 [bot:mox] todos all eligible → gate-check pre-parks 2 → simulated dispatcher recompute_ready + claim loop claims exactly 1. Full landfolk suite 116/116 pass.

Chest + tp Y came out 1 block low — embedded in the partial-height surface block. Fix: use bot terrain_top endpoint (knows block shape), fall back to inspect with bounding_box=="block" filter. Also: for entity tp, prefer surface_y + 1 not surface_y (avoid clip on uneven terrain).

(d) execute=true observed timing out at 25s even within the 16-col cap.
